reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker actively promotes paid OneCoin account activation as an opportunity to make money passively, while encouraging viewers to recruit others through a two-sided network structure. It presents investment and token-value growth claims, including that viewers can double or triple their money and that the investment can grow without doing anything, alongside instructions to pay for packages and use referral links.

citations.quote: You actually invest money. You can double, triple, you know, who knows where this will go in the next year. But you can make money with without doing absolutely anything.
You're really only building two sides, okay so everybody that goes in will go left or right
if this is sent to someone they will be automatically in your group
Please get on board.

opening.argument: Judge the investment discussion in full. The speaker says to "be wise and make a good investment and be ready to hold it," which acknowledges risk and a potentially long wait. He also says "who knows where this will go in the next year," qualifying his earlier suggestion that the investment could double or triple. Recruitment is presented as a choice, not a condition of investing: "there's no need to do the network marketing portion at all." Those qualifications support reading the pitch as speculative investment commentary, not a promise of a particular payout.

citations.quote: be wise and make a good investment and be ready to hold it
You can double, triple, you know, who knows where this will go in the next year.
there's no need to do the network marketing portion at all

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's strongest quote includes its own uncertainty: "who knows where this will go in the next year." Its two-sided placement and group-link quotes establish that a referral system is discussed, but not that every viewer must recruit to participate. The speaker expressly separates investing from network marketing. "Please get on board" is promotional language; by itself, it does not turn a qualified forecast into a guaranteed return.

citations.quote: who knows where this will go in the next year.
there's no need to do the network marketing portion at all
Please get on board.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The caution does not undo the solicitation. The speaker tells viewers they can make money "without doing absolutely anything," then describes earnings from points credited through work by an upline. Calling recruitment optional does not erase the separate pitch to earn by introducing people. The uncertainty concerns how far returns might go, while the presentation still encourages paid participation and expected gains.

citations.quote: But you can make money with without doing absolutely anything.
that's from work that you know myself and other members of our upline have already done for them
introduce this to other people, there's a huge opportunity to make some money with it

opening.argument: The video's organizing task is an account walkthrough. The speaker starts by logging into a subscriber account, directs the account holder to change a password, and shows where an activation code would be entered. He also explains where tokens would appear after redemption. A judge should distinguish showing how an interface works from establishing that its displayed balances or projected earnings are real. The procedural detail makes an operational tutorial a plausible reading of the video's primary purpose.

citations.quote: just log into One of the subscriber accounts that I set up
So just click on profile and click on main information and go in here and change your password
put the code in there redeem it and it automatically you will see your your tokens

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats the referral instructions as the whole video, but the speaker also spends time on account settings and token redemption. The cited claim that people will enter the sender's group explains what the link does; it does not, alone, establish that this walkthrough guarantees recruitment income. Likewise, "Please get on board" is an invitation, not evidence that the demonstrated steps produce the returns discussed.

put the code in there redeem it
if this is sent to someone they will be automatically in your group

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The interface walkthrough is the means of participation, not neutral instruction. The speaker urges viewers to activate quickly, walks through paying by bank wire, and offers to expedite the code after receiving payment authorization. He then explains the referral link that places new people in the viewer's group. Password-setting advice does not change that combined payment and recruitment pitch.

opening.argument: The described transaction has recognizable purchase steps: the speaker shows an upgrade area with different levels, explains bank-wire payment, and says a redeemed code results in tokens for the package purchased. That supports reading the payment as a package purchase, rather than proof on its own that funds disappear or that a promised return is paid from later buyers. The speaker also says a participant can invest without doing network marketing. The record shows a promoted product and an optional referral route; the cited material does not establish what ultimately happened to any purchaser's funds.

Tokens will just pop-up there. whatever package you purchased

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies paid activation, a two-sided network, and a link that puts invitees in the sender's group. Those details show how purchase and referrals are organized, but do not show a completed payout, a failed redemption, or where incoming payments ultimately go. The speaker's distinction between investing and networking also limits the inference that purchasing a package necessarily requires building a downline.

citations.quote: You're really only building two sides, okay so everybody that goes in will go left or right

there's no need to do the network marketing portion at all

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A completed loss is not necessary to assess what this video promotes. The speaker links account activation and package payment to tokens, claims investment can make money without work, and describes points attributed to an upline and money from introducing others. Calling the payment a purchase does not remove the promoted investment returns and recruitment-based earning mechanism.
